proof_summary: For \(p\ge7\), the hockey-stick identity and product expansions of the binomial coefficients, together with a five-block decomposition of the squared-binomial sum, give fifth-order approximations \(\binom{3p}{p}=3+a\) and \(S_2(p)=3+b\), where \(a=6pH_1-6p^2H_2\) and \(b=6pH_1+10p^3T_1\). Harmonic-sum reflection and alternating-binomial/Vandermonde identities imply \(a,b=O(p^3)\) and \(4a+3b=O(p^5)\), so \((3+a)^4(3+b)^3\equiv3^7\pmod{p^5}\); the cases \(p=3,5\) are computed directly.
